title: Anthropic's Claude Aids Mathematical Breakthrough Amid Global AI Policy Debates
body_md:
**TL;DR**

- Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge used Claude to solve the Riemann Hypothesis.
- UN talks on regulating autonomous weapons collapsed due to major power resistance.
- Rising interest in AI ethics, prompt engineering, and international governance.
- South Korean education minister resigned following an AI-assisted exam cheating scandal.

The AI landscape is currently dominated by the intersection of high-level research and urgent policy concerns. A significant breakthrough occurred as Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge utilized the Claude AI tool to solve the 166-year-old Riemann Hypothesis, a feat independently verified by the Lean and Mathlib communities. This success highlights the growing utility of AI in complex scientific discovery, even as other sectors grapple with the societal implications of the technology.

Rising discourse around AI ethics, prompt engineering, and the role of the United Nations reflects a broader push for oversight. International efforts to establish a treaty on autonomous weapons, or 'killer robots,' collapsed this week after the UN failed to reach a consensus due to resistance from major military powers. Simultaneously, public interest in AI ethics is intensifying, with discussions ranging from the psychological impact of AI companions to the human cost of automated customer service. These developments coincide with reports of AI-driven cybersecurity vulnerabilities and a high-profile academic integrity scandal in South Korea, where the education minister resigned following an AI-assisted cheating incident.
